L121@P1: SRAM for software managed scratchpads. The activations and
L122@P1: weights the NPUs operate on are typically multi-dimensional
L123@P1: tensors, mapped to a traditional, linear (1D) memory subsystem. These tensors are much larger than the scratchpad,
L124@P1: so the DMA unit blocks the activations/weights into tiles
L125@P1: and sequence them across multiple (tile) fetch operations via
L126@P1: double-buffering. As these tiles are also multi-dimensional
L127@P1: tensors, fetching them into the scratchpad involves projecting
L128@P1: the multi-dimensional coordinates into the linear space of
L129@P1: DRAM memory. A single tile is therefore decomposed into
L130@P1: minimum number of linearized memory transactions, which
L131@P1: can be up to several thousands, because a tile is sized at several
L132@P1: MBs to maximally utilize the scratchpad. Consequently, a
L133@P1: single tile fetch invokes significant bursts of page translations
L134@P1: that conventional MMUs fail to effectively capture, leading
L135@P1: to an average 95% performance overhead.

L692@P5: Overall, our data-driven analysis shows that conventional
L693@P5: MMUs which are primarily designed to capture translation
L694@P5: locality (i.e., TLBs), rather than translation throughput (i.e.,
L695@P5: number of PTWs), are inadequate in handling the translation
L696@P5: bursts in NPUs. To validate whether the TLB can be a primary
L697@P5: target for improvement in NPU MMUs, we sweep the numbers
L698@P5: of TLB entries on top of our baseline IOMMU with eight
L699@P5: hardware PTWs. Even with an unrealistically large TLB with
L700@P5: 128K entries (64× increase over baseline 2K TLB entries,
L701@P5: Table I), the NPU fails to completely filter out the bursts of
L702@P5: translation requests, achieving less than 0.02% performance
L703@P5: improvement than baseline IOMMU. Overall, we conclude
L704@P5-6: 6that NPU local TLBs, while beneficial, is not sufficiently
L705@P6: performant enough to filter out most of the translations. This
L706@P6: is because the bursts of address translations cause significant
